title: Races differ most in the parts man selects

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Races differ most in the parts man selects

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Continued selection of slight variations in one part valued by man, such as leaves, flowers or fruit, produces races that differ from each other chiefly in that part, while other parts differ only slightly.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: as a general rule, I cannot doubt that the continued selection of slight variations, either in the leaves, the flowers, or the fruit, will produce races differing from each other chiefly in these characters.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter I, “Variation under Domestication”; section “Principle of Selection anciently followed, its Effects”. Scope: cultivated plant varieties within a species

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch01-12: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Large germplasm repositories contain multi-organ traits across many cultivated varieties, and the required variance comparison is standard. Historical target labels are imperfect but enough major crops are documented for a decisive general test.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For crop varieties grouped by documented selection target, compare among-race standardized divergence in selected organs with divergence in unselected organs. Predominantly greater divergence in the selected part supports the rule; comparable divergence elsewhere refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Phenotyping protocols differ among collections.

Correlated traits may blur organ-specific effects.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.75
analysis feasibility: 0.76
data adequacy: 0.56
data existence: 0.78
operationalizability: 0.88

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Descriptor databases for cultivated plants contain the organ-level variables for a direct variance partition in major crops. Coverage and measurement quality fall off outside those crops, and correlated change is both a biological fact and a confounder of this particular contrast. A small team could run the test for well-described crops and would be extrapolating to cultivated plants as a whole.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For cultivated species, partition among-variety trait variance into the organ that breeders selected (leaf, flower, or fruit) and organs that were not the target. A larger share of variance in the selected organ would support the rule; similar variance in selected and unselected organs would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Correlation of growth predicts that selected organs will drag others along, which shrinks the expected contrast.

The identity of the historically selected organ is uncertain for many old landraces.

Genebank descriptors are often categorical, missing, and not measured with a common protocol.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data existence: 0.62
operationalizability: 0.74
data adequacy: 0.46
analysis feasibility: 0.55
